messages:
sara: FYI noticing a p99 jump for tenant acme_inc on model-redwood-1 after the runtime-validation rollout last night. p95 steady ~120ms but p99 for tiny prompts (<=16 tokens) moved 480ms -> ~1.2s. only in us-west2.

Dylan_oncall: :eyes: timeline + dashboard link? any 5xx or auth storms?

sara: https://console.redwood/metrics/tenant/acme_inc?range=1h
p95: 115->125ms
p99: 480->1.2s (sustained ~30m)
no 5xx spikes. a few auth refresh logs but nothing correlating.

nate: did the runtime-validation rollout change batching heuristics? I remember an adaptive-grace flip in that branch.

linda: confirm — runtime-validation enabled adaptive-grace on the continuous-batcher during canary. canary defaults: grace=adaptive (previously fixed 20ms), min_batch_size=1, max_batch_ms=50. promoted to prod at ~02:15 UTC.

sara: that matches the onset.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: runtime-validation v2026.02.11 canary -> promoted to prod 02:15 UTC (no rollback)

Dylan_oncall: adaptive-grace can increase hold times for low-entropy / tiny prompts under bursty arrivals. suspect keyed coalescer waiting behavior -> tail inflation. Need repro and quick mitigation.

kim_research: I'll try a lightweight repro against the same route with microbursts + small gaps.

kim_research: ```
# tiny-burst-repro.py
import requests, time
URL = "https://api.redwood/v1/generate?tenant=acme_inc&model=model-redwood-1"
for i in range(1200):
    requests.post(URL, json={"input":"ok"})
    time.sleep(0.005 if i%8!=0 else 0.11)
```

kim_research: staging w/ adaptive-grace shows p99 ~1.05s for same pattern. disabling adaptive drops p99 to ~480-520ms. reproducible locally.

nate: good repro. two mitigation paths: per-route override to tighten grace_ms, or rollback the global change. override is faster and lower blast radius.

linda: proposing per-route patch: keep batching enabled but force short hold for this tenant/route. PATCH via config API: ```PATCH /v1/config/routes/acme_inc/model-redwood-1 { "continuous_batching": { "enabled": true, "grace_ms": 4, "min_batch_size": 2 } }```

sara: do the override. minimal blast radius and we can monitor.

ops-bot: config-service: patch accepted, propagating to us-west2 nodes 02:52 UTC
deploy-bot: config rolled to 12/12 nodes in us-west2 02:54 UTC
support-bot: ticket #102134 updated: mitigation applied, customer notified.

Dylan_oncall: watching a short canary window (10m).

sara: p99 settled back to ~520ms within ~6 minutes after propagation. p95 unchanged. mitigation effective.

kim_research: preliminary root cause: adaptive-grace's keyed coalescer increases per-key hold windows to improve throughput. with many tiny, low-entropy prompts and bursty arrivals some keys don't fill quickly; the adaptive algorithm lengthens holds for those keys which pushes out the tail. KV-cache hits increase skew across keys, so hotspots are fast but many other keys sit waiting longer.

nate: follow-ups / action items:
- keep per-route override for acme_inc until we add a regression test and evaluate adaptive defaults (linda)
- add CI regression that simulates microburst + tiny prompts to catch tail regressions for continuous-batcher changes (kim_research)
- write a short oncall runbook: detect this pattern and apply per-route override (sara)
- platform owners to review adaptive-grace thresholds and add telemetry for per-key hold distributions (dylan_oncall)

linda: override left in place and annotated with root cause link to this thread.

ops-bot: infra note created: infra-2026-3467

kim_research: collected coalescer perf flamegraphs from staging showing increased timer wakeups per-core and wider distribution of per-key hold durations; attached to ticket.

support-bot: acme_inc support rep confirmed improvement after mitigation (customer-facing ack at 03:10 UTC).

sara: closing monitoring loop — p99 stable now. I'll draft a 1-pager explaining throughput vs tail tradeoffs and recommended route overrides for latency-sensitive tenants. will attach CI repro and runbook to the infra ticket.

Dylan_oncall: thumbs-up. once CI test + runbook exist we can safely re-evaluate adaptive-grace defaults. for now targeted overrides + customer comms are the right call.
